newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr expected to trim overnight gains vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr expected to trim overnight gains vs yen.

text.p: The dollar is expected to trim overnight gains against the yen during Asian trading time on Wednesday as exporters are expected to emerge on topside, limiting its further rise, dealers said.

Germany's planned statement calling for a strong mark and a strong euro later in day is expected to weigh on dollar/mark after hitting a 71-month high overnight, but buying interest is likely to emerge on dips, they added.
The dollar rose to a peak of 1.8040 marks in New York, its highest since August 1991, on fresh signs that Europe's proposed single currency may be a weak one.
The greenback also edged higher towards 116 yen overnight, a level Tokyo traders have not seen since late June.
"This is a level where market participants would like to start morning trade by selling," a city bank dealer said.
Dealers said exporters, who have sold dollars at lower levels recently, are likely to kick in dollar sales on the topside.
"I will watch closely how eagar exporters and Japanese investors are to sell dollars for yen for hedging purposes on the topside," a trust bank dealer said.
In New York, the dollar's strong rally against the mark lost steam after Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler told reporters in Germany that the dollar's rally may have become excessive.

Zeitler added that Germany wants a strong mark and German Finance Minister Theo Waigel later told Reuters the German cabinet will make a statement on Wednesday calling for a strong mark and a strong euro.
Dealers said they would remain cautious over comments from German monetary authorities. "But buying interest on dips is still intact in dollar/mark," the trust bank dealer said.

In dollar/yen trade, the city bank dealer said that although he was not sure if the dollar is now entering a new trading range, traders may be keen to buy the dollar on dips on the back of strong fundamental factors in the United States.
